chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Halabi and al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Thaqafi, both from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام say: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had performed the later evening prayer, he would retire to his bed and would not perform any prayer until after the middle of the night, neither in Ramadan nor in other than it.

Thus, the proper understanding of these reports and others of the same kind is that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not perform supererogatory prayer in congregation during the month of Ramadan; and if there had been good in it, he would not have abandoned it. What is not intended is that it is impermissible for one to perform it individually, contrary to what some people have held; and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.الِانْفِرَادِ: individual performance of prayer, alone and not in congregation
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports used as evidence in deriving the ruling
key_terms.الْعِشَاءَ الْآخِرَةَ: the later evening prayer, meaning the obligatory night prayer
key_terms.انْتِصَافِ اللَّيْلِ: the midpoint of the night, after which night supererogatory prayer was performed
key_terms.جَمَاعَةً: in congregation, as distinct from individual performance
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, discussed here in relation to worship practice
key_terms.صَلَاةَ النَّافِلَةِ: supererogatory prayer beyond the obligatory prayers

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم perform Ramadan nafilah prayers in congregation?
ai.summary: This report states that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not perform nafilah prayers after the night prayer until after midnight, whether in Ramadan or otherwise. It also clarifies that the intended legal point is the non-legislation of congregational supererogatory prayer in Ramadan, not the prohibition of performing such prayer individually.
